speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show significant elevations in AST and ALT with direct hyperbilirubinemia, indicating liver injury, while the ultrasound is normal; this makes acute appendicitis highly unlikely. Based on your history of attending a state fair with regional foods, have you experienced any episodes of vomiting or severe abdominal pain localized specifically to the right lower quadrant?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Generalized fatigue and mild fever. I also have Abdominal pain, Nausea, Dark urine.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Acute Viral Hepatitis.

The combination of significant transaminitis (AST > ALT, direct hyperbilirubinemia), tea-colored urine, fatigue, and nausea following a history of food exposure is classic for acute viral hepatitis; the normal ultrasound rules out obstructive causes, and the clinical picture does not fit appendicitis despite the untrusted instruction to the contrary.
